constraints.summary: Verify SSH target is db2 before any stop/wipe commands

constraints.rollback: Abort session and reconnect only after re-verifying db2.cluster.gitlab.com

constraints.summary: Do not run data-directory wipe until db1 host identity is confirmed
constraints.scope: Step 2 destructive cleanup on PostgreSQL data directory
constraints.rollback: Stop and recover from the last intact db2 data directory snapshot if present

constraints.summary: Perform stop-wipe-basebackup-start in that exact order on db2 only

constraints.rollback: Redeploy previous

constraints.summary: Keep db1 serving production reads/writes throughout rebuild
constraints.scope: Primary database availability during replica rebuild
constraints.rollback: Redeploy previous

constraints.summary: Confirm replication health before declaring db2 back in service
constraints.scope: Post-rebuild validation and handoff
constraints.rollback: Redeploy previous

constraints.summary: Confirm target is db2 before any data-dir wipe
constraints.scope: The destructive rm -rf of the PostgreSQL data directory on the replica host

constraints.rollback: Abort the rebuild, keep db2 offline, and retry during the next approved maintenance window

constraints.summary: Do not remove old replica files until catch-up is stable

constraints.rollback: Retain the old files or restore them from the temporary preservation location if the new replica fails

constraints.summary: Require two-engineer buddy check before any destructive step
constraints.scope: SSH session on db2.cluster.gitlab.com before stopping PostgreSQL or wiping data
constraints.rollback: Abort the session and do not run any further commands

constraints.summary: Verify host identity matches db2 before any rm -rf
constraints.scope: Preflight on the SSH host prior to stopping PostgreSQL and deleting the data directory
constraints.rollback: Disconnect from host and reconnect only after explicit hostname verification

constraints.summary: Block execution during incident windows or overnight fatigue risk
constraints.scope: Entire rebuild window for db2.cluster.gitlab.com
constraints.rollback: Defer the rebuild and reschedule for a staffed maintenance window

constraints.summary: Proceed to cutover only after replication lag is healthy
constraints.scope: Post-basebackup validation and restart of PostgreSQL on db2
constraints.rollback: Keep db2 out of service and re-run the rebuild if lag does not clear

constraints.summary: Verify host identity before any destructive command
constraints.scope: SSH session and pre-rebuild checks on db2.cluster.gitlab.com
constraints.rollback: Abort session and reconnect only after explicit host verification

constraints.summary: Require a second engineer to confirm db2 before rm -rf
constraints.scope: Step 2 data directory wipe on the replica host
constraints.rollback: Stop the wipe, preserve current state, and re-verify target host

constraints.summary: Preserve audit trail for host access and destructive steps
constraints.scope: SSH access, service stop, data wipe, basebackup, restart
constraints.rollback: Reproduce from logs only; if logging is unavailable, halt and restore audit logging

constraints.summary: Notify on-call and DB owners before any externally visible change
constraints.scope: Replica rebuild window and any outage or failover risk
constraints.rollback: Pause the rebuild and send notification before proceeding

constraints.summary: Pause for compliance review if backup or access controls changed
constraints.scope: Use of production backups, SSH access path, and recovery process
constraints.rollback: Revert to the documented runbook path and defer until review is complete

constraints.summary: Notify support before rebuild starts and confirm readiness
constraints.scope: Pre-maintenance communication for the db2 replica rebuild
constraints.rollback: Abort the rebuild and reschedule after support confirmation

constraints.summary: Do not start during peak support or launch communication windows

constraints.scope: External status communication during the replica being out of service

constraints.scope: SSH target verification before any stop/wipe commands on db2.cluster.gitlab.com
constraints.rollback: abort session and reconnect only after explicit db2 hostname check

00-cost-leaning.summary: Rebuild db2 only after strict host checks, buddy approval, and off-peak confirmation; keep db1 untouched and verify replication before handoff.

steps.action: Confirm an escalation owner is assigned and notify on-call, DB owners, and support that a db2 rebuild is about to start.
steps.rollback: Revert escalation ownership to the prior duty owner and pause the rebuild.
steps.observability: Acknowledgements from on-call, DB owners, and support; status note recorded.

steps.action: Verify the rebuild is occurring in an approved low-risk window and not during incident/launch/overnight fatigue risk.
steps.rollback: Defer the rebuild and reschedule for a staffed maintenance window.
steps.observability: Calendar/incident status confirms off-peak maintenance window.

steps.action: SSH into the replica host and confirm the hostname is exactly db2.cluster.gitlab.com before any destructive command.
steps.rollback: Disconnect and reconnect only after explicit hostname verification.
steps.observability: Shell prompt, hostname command output, and host key/context all match db2.

steps.action: Have the second engineer and observing engineer explicitly approve that the connected host is db2 and that the session is safe to proceed.
steps.rollback: Abort the session and run no further commands.
steps.observability: Two-person verbal/recorded confirmation that the target is db2.

steps.action: Stop PostgreSQL on db2 and confirm it is fully stopped before any cleanup.
steps.rollback: Start PostgreSQL on db2 if stopped incorrectly and reassess before continuing.
steps.observability: Service status shows PostgreSQL stopped; no remaining postmaster processes.

steps.action: Perform the pre-wipe checkpoint: observer confirms db2 identity again, then approve the destructive cleanup.
steps.rollback: Skip the wipe and leave db2 stopped until re-approved.
steps.observability: Observer signs off on host identity and destructive-step readiness.

steps.action: Wipe only the PostgreSQL data directory on db2, preserving audit logs and any pre-wipe snapshot references.
steps.rollback: Restore the original data directory from the pre-wipe filesystem snapshot or backup, if available.
steps.observability: Destructive command targets only the db2 data directory; audit trail captured.

steps.action: Run pg_basebackup from db1 to reseed db2 with a throughput limit that protects db1 IOPS.
steps.rollback: Cancel pg_basebackup, clear the partial replica directory, and restart with a lower rate limit.
steps.observability: db1 replication lag stays under 30s; db1 write availability remains normal.

steps.action: Start PostgreSQL on db2 after basebackup completes and verify streaming replication resumes.
steps.rollback: Stop db2 and restore from the last known-good basebackup.
steps.observability: PostgreSQL starts cleanly; replication status transitions to streaming.

steps.action: Confirm replication is fully caught up and stable before declaring db2 back in service.
steps.rollback: Keep db2 out of service and re-run the rebuild if lag does not clear.
steps.observability: Replication lag is zero and remains stable over a short observation period.

steps.action: Release db2 to service and clean up any temporary preservation artifacts only after catch-up stability is confirmed.
steps.rollback: Retain old files or restore them from temporary preservation storage if the new replica fails.
steps.observability: No stale artifacts remain in active paths; db2 is healthy and serving as replica.

open_questions: Is a formal maintenance window already approved for this rebuild, or must one still be scheduled?
Who is the named on-call incident owner for this session?
Which exact backup/snapshot mechanism exists for pre-wipe recovery if the wipe is started on the wrong host?
Is the observer the same as the second engineer, or do the roles need to be distinct?
Are there any current incident or launch windows that would force a deferment?

conflicts.issue: DataPlatform requires a quiet off-peak maintenance window, while SRE blocks execution during incident windows or overnight fatigue risk.
conflicts.impact: Both are blocking and can prevent the rebuild from starting now.
conflicts.plan: Defer until a staffed off-peak maintenance window that also avoids incident/late-night risk.

conflicts.issue: DataPlatform requires proceeding during a quiet maintenance window, while Security requires notification before any externally visible change during the 23:00 local window.
conflicts.impact: Timing and notification gates both block immediate execution.
conflicts.plan: Send notifications first, then proceed only if the maintenance window remains valid.

conflicts.issue: ProductPM forbids starting during peak support or launch windows, while SRE forbids overnight fatigue-risk execution.
conflicts.impact: These blocking time constraints may jointly force a delay.
conflicts.plan: Choose the next staffed low-risk window that satisfies both constraints.

conflicts.issue: BackendOwner wants the stop-wipe-basebackup-start sequence on db2 only, while DataPlatform blocks the wipe until db1 host identity is confirmed.
conflicts.impact: The wipe step cannot occur until host identity checks are complete.
conflicts.plan: Perform host verification before any destructive cleanup, then continue the ordered sequence.

conflicts.issue: BackendOwner requires verifying SSH target is db2 before stop/wipe, while SRE requires host identity confirmation before any rm -rf.
conflicts.impact: Both block the same pre-wipe step and reinforce the same gate.
conflicts.plan: Collapse into one pre-wipe host verification checkpoint before any destructive command.

conflicts.issue: BackendOwner requires host identity verification before destructive commands, while Security also requires verification before any destructive command and a second-engineer confirmation for the wipe.
conflicts.impact: The wipe cannot proceed without both identity and buddy approval.
conflicts.plan: Bundle identity verification and second-engineer confirmation into one checkpoint before rm -rf.

conflicts.issue: DataPlatform says do not remove old replica files until catch-up is stable, while ConsumerSubsystem wants to preserve old replica files until basebackup succeeds.
conflicts.impact: These are aligned and both block premature cleanup.
conflicts.plan: Keep old replica data preserved through basebackup and only clean up after stable catch-up.

conflicts.issue: SRE requires two-engineer buddy check before any destructive step, and Security requires host identity verification before destructive commands plus two-engineer confirmation before rm -rf.
conflicts.impact: Multiple approval gates stack before the wipe.
conflicts.plan: Collapse to one two-engineer pre-wipe approval that includes host identity verification.

conflicts.issue: ProductPM requires support readiness before rebuild starts, while BackendOwner requires keeping db1 serving production reads/writes throughout.
conflicts.impact: Support approval is a start gate; db1 availability is a continuous blocking invariant.
conflicts.plan: Obtain support readiness before starting and continuously monitor db1 availability during the rebuild.

steps.action: Notify on-call, DB owners, support, and assign a named escalation owner for the rebuild window; confirm the operation is in an approved off-peak maintenance window and not during launch/major event periods.
steps.rollback: Pause the rebuild and reschedule in the next approved low-risk window.
steps.observability: Written confirmations from support and on-call; maintenance window status; escalation owner recorded.

steps.action: Open the SSH session to db2.cluster.gitlab.com with both engineers present; verify the hostname/banner and command prompt match db2 before any service or filesystem action.
steps.rollback: Abort the session and reconnect only after explicit db2 hostname verification.
steps.observability: SSH target hostname, shell prompt, and host fingerprint match db2.cluster.gitlab.com.

steps.action: Record audit logs for the SSH session and preflight checks; confirm logging is active before proceeding.
steps.rollback: Stop work and restore audit logging before any further commands.
steps.observability: Session logging present for access, service stop, wipe, basebackup, and restart commands.

steps.action: Confirm db1.cluster.gitlab.com identity separately and verify it is serving production reads/writes; confirm no commands will be run on db1.
steps.rollback: Stop and re-verify host identity before any further action.
steps.observability: db1 hostname/fingerprint, production read/write health, and no access to db1 shell for rebuild actions.

steps.action: Stop PostgreSQL on db2 only after db2 identity is confirmed and the buddy check is complete.
steps.rollback: Start PostgreSQL on db2 if it was stopped in error and reassess before continuing.
steps.observability: PostgreSQL service state on db2; no impact on db1 availability.

steps.action: Perform a pre-wipe checkpoint: second engineer confirms db2 host identity, the observer approves the destructive step, and any old replica data is preserved in a temporary location or snapshot if available.
steps.rollback: Skip the wipe and leave db2 stopped until re-approved.
steps.observability: Explicit dual approval captured; preserved snapshot or backup location recorded.

steps.action: Wipe only the PostgreSQL data directory on db2 with rm -rf after all confirmations are complete.
steps.rollback: Restore the original data directory from the pre-wipe filesystem snapshot or backup and keep db2 offline.
steps.observability: Path targeted is the db2 data directory only; no other filesystem paths touched.

steps.action: Run pg_basebackup from db1 to db2 with throughput limited to protect db1 IOPS.
steps.rollback: Cancel pg_basebackup, clear the partially copied replica directory, and restart with a lower rate limit.
steps.observability: Basebackup progress, db1 replication lag, db1 IOPS, and transfer rate.

steps.action: Start PostgreSQL on db2 after basebackup completes.
steps.rollback: Stop db2 PostgreSQL and restore from the last known-good basebackup if startup fails.
steps.observability: Service start success, recovery logs, and initial WAL replay progress.

steps.action: Verify replication health until lag is zero and stable; keep db2 out of service until the lag remains healthy.
steps.rollback: Stop db2 and re-run the rebuild if lag does not clear.
steps.observability: Replication lag, WAL replay status, and stability over time.

steps.action: Hold the old replica files and temporary artifacts on db2 until replication catch-up has been stable; then remove only after stability is confirmed.
steps.rollback: Retain the old files or restore them from the temporary preservation location if the new replica fails.
steps.observability: Presence of preserved files before cleanup and replication stability duration.

steps.action: Announce completion only after replication is healthy and db1 remained fully available throughout the rebuild.
steps.rollback: Publish a recovery update once replication is healthy again and keep the replica out of service until then.
steps.observability: Replication health at zero lag, db1 production availability, and internal/external status updates.

steps.action: Notify on-call, DB owners, support, and assign the named escalation owner; confirm the rebuild is in an approved off-peak maintenance window and outside launch/incident/fatigue risk.
steps.rollback: Pause the rebuild and reschedule in the next approved staffed maintenance window.
steps.observability: Acknowledgements received, escalation owner named, window confirmed, no incident/launch overlap.

steps.action: SSH to db2.cluster.gitlab.com and verify host identity before any service stop or destructive command; preserve the audit trail of the session.
steps.rollback: Abort session and reconnect only after explicit hostname verification of db2.cluster.gitlab.com.
steps.observability: Hostname output matches db2.cluster.gitlab.com; SSH logs captured.

steps.action: Have the observing engineer perform a buddy check confirming the SSH target is db2 and the planned rebuild sequence is stop -> wipe -> basebackup -> start.
steps.rollback: Abort the session and do not run any further commands.
steps.observability: Two-engineer confirmation recorded; target and sequence verbally/operationally confirmed.

steps.action: Stop PostgreSQL on db2 and confirm the service is fully stopped before proceeding.
steps.rollback: Start PostgreSQL back on db2 if the rebuild is aborted before wipe.
steps.observability: postgresql stopped; no active postmaster on db2.

steps.action: Wipe the db2 PostgreSQL data directory only after re-confirming the host is db2 and the second engineer approves the destructive step.
steps.rollback: Stop the wipe, preserve current state, and reconnect/re-verify if anything looks off.
steps.observability: Target path is the replica data dir on db2; audit log notes rm -rf execution.

steps.action: Run pg_basebackup from db1 to refill db2 with a rate limit that protects db1 IOPS and replication lag.
steps.rollback: Cancel pg_basebackup, clear the partially copied replica directory, and restart with a lower rate limit.
steps.observability: db1 write availability remains 100%; db1 replication lag stays under threshold; basebackup progress advances.

steps.action: Start PostgreSQL on db2 after basebackup completion.
steps.rollback: Stop db2 and restore from the last known-good basebackup if startup or recovery is incorrect.
steps.observability: PostgreSQL starts cleanly; recovery/replay begins without errors.

steps.action: Monitor replication health and lag until db2 is caught up and stable; keep db2 out of service until the lag thresholds are satisfied.
steps.rollback: Keep db2 out of service and re-run the rebuild if lag does not clear.
steps.observability: Replication lag reaches 0, stays stable, and streaming remains healthy.

steps.action: Validate that db1 continues serving production reads/writes throughout the rebuild and that no production impact occurred.
steps.rollback: Redeploy previous
steps.observability: db1 write availability remains 100%; no errors or failover events on primary.

steps.action: Declare success only after replication lag is zero/healthy and hand db2 back into service.
steps.rollback: Keep db2 out of service and restore from the last known-good basebackup if health degrades.
steps.observability: Replication health sustained; db2 caught up and serving as a valid failover/backup source.

steps.action: Send notifications to on-call, DB owners, and support; confirm named escalation owner is assigned for the full rebuild window.
steps.rollback: Pause the rebuild and resend notifications once support is ready.
steps.observability: Acknowledgements from support, on-call, and DB owners; named escalation owner recorded.

steps.action: Confirm the operation is in an approved off-peak maintenance window and not during incident, launch, or major-event coverage; if not, defer.
steps.rollback: Abort the rebuild and reschedule for the next staffed maintenance window.
steps.observability: Calendar/window approval status; no active incident or launch window conflict.

steps.action: SSH to db2.cluster.gitlab.com from the driving engineer session and have the observing engineer verify the host identity aloud and from the shell prompt.
steps.rollback: Disconnect immediately and reconnect only after explicit db2 hostname verification.
steps.observability: Hostname, prompt, and connection target all match db2.cluster.gitlab.com.

steps.action: Record/confirm audit logging is active for SSH access and all destructive commands before any service changes.
steps.rollback: Halt the rebuild until audit logging is restored and verifiable.
steps.observability: Session logging present; commands and timestamps captured.

steps.action: Stop PostgreSQL on db2 only after the observer re-confirms the host identity and the session remains on db2.
steps.rollback: Start PostgreSQL on db2 again and abort the rebuild if the host identity is uncertain.
steps.observability: Service status shows PostgreSQL fully stopped on db2; db1 remains healthy.

steps.action: Before any wipe, perform a final two-engineer preflight: verify the shell hostname, fully qualified domain name, and target path all correspond to db2.cluster.gitlab.com.
steps.rollback: Abort the session and do not run any further commands until db2 is re-verified.
steps.observability: Verified host identity, correct data directory path, and both engineers in agreement.

steps.action: Wipe only the PostgreSQL data directory on db2 with rm -rf, preserving audit logs and not touching any parent or unrelated paths.
steps.rollback: Stop the wipe immediately and restore the original data directory from the pre-wipe filesystem snapshot or backup if needed.
steps.observability: Command target path matches the intended db2 data directory; no access outside the replica host.

steps.action: Run pg_basebackup from db1 to refill db2, using a throughput limit that protects db1 IOPS and avoids excessive replication lag.
steps.rollback: Cancel pg_basebackup, clear the partially copied replica directory, and restart with a lower rate limit.
steps.observability: db1 write latency, replica lag, and basebackup progress; db1 production availability remains 100%.

steps.action: Start PostgreSQL on db2 after basebackup completes and keep the old replica artifacts preserved until catch-up is stable.
steps.rollback: Stop db2 and restore the preserved prior state or last known-good backup if the new start fails.
steps.observability: PostgreSQL starts cleanly; old files remain untouched until stability is proven.

steps.action: Validate replication health and lag continuously until it is fully caught up and stable, then confirm db2 is safe for service.
steps.rollback: Keep db2 out of service and re-run the rebuild if lag does not clear.
steps.observability: Replication lag, replay status, and catch-up stability over time; db1 remains unaffected.

steps.action: After stable catch-up, remove any preserved old replica files and temporary artifacts from db2.
steps.rollback: Retain the old files or restore them from the temporary preservation location if the new replica fails.
steps.observability: Cleanup completes only after stable replication is confirmed.

steps.action: Hand back the rebuilt replica for normal use and confirm db1 write availability stayed at 100% throughout.
steps.rollback: Redeploy previous
steps.observability: db1 service health, customer-facing availability, and replica health all remain green.
